name: A181568 / Stormer 101-smooth pairs: find a term > 941747621709311 or prove completeness
compute_profile: needs cluster for planning purposes. Full discovery and replay costs are unmeasured. Start with a bounded pilot using compact Pell representations.
statement: OEIS A181568 lists positive integers k such that the largest prime factor of k^2 - 1 is 101 (equivalently, k - 1 and k + 1 are both 101-smooth and 101 divides k^2 - 1). Størmer’s theorem gives finiteness for these smooth pairs, as reflected by the OEIS keyword fini. Florian Luca and Filip Najman (arXiv:1005.1533; Math. Comp. 80, 2011) determined all x such that P(x^2 - 1) < 100 (stopping strictly below 101; companion OEIS A175607 stops at n = 25, p = 97, where p = 79 reaches 19182937474703818751 > 10^19). The b-file lists 3,340 terms below 10^17. OEIS credits David A. Corneth for the table and Klaus Brockhaus for its first 2,325 entries. The last listed term is a(3340) = 941747621709311, and Corneth asks whether there is a larger term. Writing k^2 - 1 = D y^2 with D > 1 squarefree and 101-smooth (and y 101-smooth) maps every term to a solution (k, y) of the Pell equation x^2 - D y^2 = 1 across all 2^26 - 1 = 67,108,863 squarefree 101-smooth integers D > 1. Note that requiring k^2 - 1 to be even misses k = 100. Requiring 101 | D misses cases with positive even v_101(k^2 - 1), where 101 divides y and is absent from D. The analogous example for p = 7 is k = 97, with 97^2 - 1 = 2^6 * 3 * 7^2 and D = 3.
success_criterion: CONFIRMED: EITHER (a) an explicit integer k > 941747621709311 together with the complete factorization of k - 1 and k + 1 over the 26 primes <= 101 (certifying every prime factor <= 101 and 101 | k^2 - 1); OR (b) a complete, dual-verified Stormer-Pell exhaustive proof over all 2^26 - 1 = 67,108,863 squarefree 101-smooth integers D > 1 — paired with an explicit, independently audited (or Lean 4 kernel-checked) proof of the solution-index bound used by the search. Luca and Najman’s Section 2 gives a conservative bound m <= 102 for primes up to 101: if m > 12, the Lucas quotient y_m/y_1 has a primitive prime divisor q congruent to ±1 modulo m, and q <= 101 implies m <= 102 — proving that 941747621709311 is the exact maximum term of A181568. Calibration: reproduce all 3,340 published terms in OEIS b181568.txt and Luca-Najman's A175607(1..25) maxima for p <= 97. Before claiming, recheck OEIS A181568 and A175607 to confirm no larger term or completeness proof has appeared.
verification_method: For a witness k > 941747621709311: verify k > 941747621709311 in exact arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic, factor k - 1 and k + 1 completely by trial division over the 26 primes <= 101, verify the prime-power products reconstruct k - 1 and k + 1 exactly, and verify 101 | (k^2 - 1). For a completeness proof: audit the solution-index bound and run two independent Pell enumerations across all 2^26 - 1 = 67,108,863 squarefree 101-smooth D > 1 (certifying the fundamental solutions or justified exclusions, and accounting for every index up to the proven bound), confirming both reproduce A175607(1..25) and output the exact same 3,340 terms of A181568 <= 941747621709311. Certificates exceeding 1 MB follow kit/SUBMIT.md section 1.
angles: Pilot Luca and Najman’s compact Pell representations and modular smoothness tests. Certify that any regulator multiple used in the computation cannot cause a solution to be missed. Use exact continued fractions for small cases and for bounded fundamental-solution checks.
A search for witnesses can prioritize the 2^25 values of D divisible by 101. For completeness, include the D not divisible by 101 to cover positive even exponents of 101 in k^2 - 1.
Benchmark throughput on the 2^4 - 1 = 15 squarefree 7-smooth D > 1 and the p <= 73 subset first.
pitfalls: Compare any candidate with the b-file. A verified candidate above the listed maximum but below 10^17 would correct the reported coverage.

Do NOT restrict to x^2 - 2 d y^2 = 1 or 101 | D: that misses even k (e.g. a(1) = 100 where k^2 - 1 = 9999 is odd) and misses terms where v_101(k^2 - 1) is positive and even (so 101 | y rather than 101 | D, as in 97^2 - 1 = 2^6 * 3 * 7^2 for p = 7).

Ordinary continued fractions that build the full fundamental solutions were already impractical for the earlier bound below 100. Audit any compact solver and its completeness argument against the corrected Luca–Najman paper and the published erratum.
